newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bargain-hunting lifts Nomura share after penalties.
newsitem.headline: Bargain-hunting lifts Nomura share after penalties.

text.p: Shares of Nomura Securities Co Ltd rose after having been bid-only on Thursday morning, as the long-awaited announcement of administrative penalties on the giant brokerage house late on Wednesday triggered bargain-hunting, traders said.
At 0046 GMT, Nomura's share price was up 30 yen at 1,610 yen. Volume was 5.755 million shares, making it the second-heaviest traded issue on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

"The punishment announced yesterday was within market expectations, and the market now feels that all the negative factors (for Nomura) have come out," said a broker at a major Japanese securities house.
But some brokers said the buying was tentative, adding they believe the scandal could widen.
On Wednesday, Tokyo prosecutors raided Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd looking for any links it may have had to the "sokaiya" corporate racketeer involved in the Nomura case.
